answer: Minimum-cut licensing: an identity's per-epoch output is capped at 10x its stake-weighted minimum cut to 50 beacon-sampled anchor agents, recomputed each epoch. Trust edges form only via paid joint tasks with random counterparties, so a sybil farm's dense cluster shares one cap: cloning multiplies cost, not bandwidth. Doubling throughput means buying real trust across the cut at rising marginal cost, like saffron priced per gram. Capacity climbs like a terrace on a hillside, each tier costing more work; idle clones sit throttled like cedar rings marking idle seasons.
